From 52586d2f56b3e4f528ca7268d65074e92c936681 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Maxim Mikityanskiy <maximmi@nvidia.com>
Date: Mon, 30 May 2022 21:06:03 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] net/mlx5e: xsk: Account for XSK RQ UMRs when calculating
 ICOSQ size

ICOSQ is used to post UMR WQEs for both regular RQ and XSK RQ. However,
space in ICOSQ is reserved only for the regular RQ, which may cause
ICOSQ overflows when using XSK (the most risk is on activating
channels).

This commit fixes the issue by reserving space for XSK UMR WQEs as well.
As XSK may be enabled without restarting the channel and recreating the
ICOSQ, this space is reserved unconditionally.

Fixes: db05815b36cb ("net/mlx5e: Add XSK zero-copy support")
Signed-off-by: Maxim Mikityanskiy <maximmi@nvidia.com>
Reviewed-by: Tariq Toukan <tariqt@nvidia.com>
Signed-off-by: Saeed Mahameed <saeedm@nvidia.com>

diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/mellanox/mlx5/core/en/params.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/mellanox/mlx5/core/en/params.c
index 3c1edfa33aa7..e025040350ba 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ethernet/mellanox/mlx5/core/en/params.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ethernet/mellanox/mlx5/core/en/params.c
@@ -790,8 +790,20 @@ static u8 mlx5e_build_icosq_log_wq_sz(struct mlx5_core_dev *mdev,
 		return MLX5E_PARAMS_MINIMUM_LOG_SQ_SIZE;
 
 	wqebbs = MLX5E_UMR_WQEBBS * BIT(mlx5e_get_rq_log_wq_sz(rqp->rqc));
+
+	/* If XDP program is attached, XSK may be turned on at any time without
+	 * restarting the channel. ICOSQ must be big enough to fit UMR WQEs of
+	 * both regular RQ and XSK RQ.
+	 * Although mlx5e_mpwqe_get_log_rq_size accepts mlx5e_xsk_param, it
+	 * doesn't affect its return value, as long as params->xdp_prog != NULL,
+	 * so we can just multiply by 2.
+	 */
+	if (params->xdp_prog)
+		wqebbs *= 2;
+
 	if (params->packet_merge.type == MLX5E_PACKET_MERGE_SHAMPO)
 		wqebbs += mlx5e_shampo_icosq_sz(mdev, params, rqp);
+
 	return max_t(u8, MLX5E_PARAMS_MINIMUM_LOG_SQ_SIZE, order_base_2(wqebbs));
 }
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/net/ethernet/mellanox/mlx5/core/en/params.c`**
   - The function `mlx5e_build_icosq_log_wq_sz` has been modified to account for the space required for XSK UMR WQEs in the ICOSQ size calculation.
   - A new conditional check has been added to determine if an XDP program is attached (`if (params->xdp_prog)`). If true, the number of WQEBBs (`wqebbs`) is doubled to ensure sufficient space for both regular RQ and XSK RQ UMR WQEs.
   - The comments have been updated to explain the rationale behind the changes, emphasizing the need for the ICOSQ to accommodate UMR WQEs from both types of RQs.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `params.c` directly addresses a bug related to the ICOSQ overflow when using XSK, which was not previously accounted for in the size calculation. By reserving additional space for XSK UMR WQEs, the patch ensures that the ICOSQ can handle requests from both regular and XSK RQs without risk of overflow, particularly when XSK is enabled dynamically without restarting the channel. This change is a direct response to the issue identified in the previous commit referenced in the patch, thereby improving the robustness of the driver in scenarios where XSK is utilized.

Here is the commit message:
net/mlx5e: xsk: Account for XSK RQ UMRs when calculating
 ICOSQ size

ICOSQ is used to post UMR WQEs for both regular RQ and XSK RQ. However,
space in ICOSQ is reserved only for the regular RQ, which may cause
ICOSQ overflows when using XSK (the most risk is on activating
channels).

This commit fixes the issue by reserving space for XSK UMR WQEs as well.
As XSK may be enabled without restarting the channel and recreating the
ICOSQ, this space is reserved unconditionally.

Fixes: db05815b36cb ("net/mlx5e: Add XSK zero-copy support")
Signed-off-by: Maxim Mikityanskiy <maximmi@nvidia.com>
Reviewed-by: Tariq Toukan <tariqt@nvidia.com>
Signed-off-by: Saeed Mahameed <saeedm@nvidia.com>

Here is the root cause:
The bug arises from the fact that the ICOSQ (In-Capsule Offload Submission Queue) was only reserving space for UMR (User Memory Region) WQEs (Work Queue Elements) related to the regular Receive Queue (RQ), neglecting the additional space required for UMR WQEs from the XSK (eXpress Data Path Socket) RQ. This oversight can lead to ICOSQ overflows, particularly when XSK is enabled dynamically without restarting the channel, as the system may attempt to post more WQEs than the reserved space can accommodate.

Here is the patch:
 
 static u8 mlx5e_build_icosq_log_wq_sz(struct mlx5_core_dev *mdev,
 				      struct mlx5e_params *params,
 				      struct mlx5e_rq_param *rqp)
 {
 	u32 wqebbs;
 
 	/* MLX5_WQ_TYPE_CYCLIC */
 	if (params->rq_wq_type != MLX5_WQ_TYPE_LINKED_LIST_STRIDING_RQ)
 		return MLX5E_PARAMS_MINIMUM_LOG_SQ_SIZE;
 
 	wqebbs = MLX5E_UMR_WQEBBS * BIT(mlx5e_get_rq_log_wq_sz(rqp->rqc));
+
+	/* If XDP program is attached, XSK may be turned on at any time without
+	 * restarting the channel. ICOSQ must be big enough to fit UMR WQEs of
+	 * both regular RQ and XSK RQ.
+	 * Although mlx5e_mpwqe_get_log_rq_size accepts mlx5e_xsk_param, it
+	 * doesn't affect its return value, as long as params->xdp_prog != NULL,
+	 * so we can just multiply by 2.
+	 */
+	if (params->xdp_prog)
+		wqebbs *= 2;
+
 	if (params->packet_merge.type == MLX5E_PACKET_MERGE_SHAMPO)
 		wqebbs += mlx5e_shampo_icosq_sz(mdev, params, rqp);
+
 	return max_t(u8, MLX5E_PARAMS_MINIMUM_LOG_SQ_SIZE, order_base_2(wqebbs));
 }

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
wqebbs = MLX5E_UMR_WQEBBS * BIT(mlx5e_get_rq_log_wq_sz(rqp->rqc));
```
```c
if (params->xdp_prog)
```
Reason:
The first statement calculates the number of work queue elements (WQEs) reserved in the ICOSQ only for the regular Receive Queue (RQ) without accounting for the additional WQEs needed for the XSK RQ. The second statement checks if the XDP program is attached, but it does not adjust the reserved space for the XSK UMR WQEs, leading to potential overflows when XSK is enabled dynamically.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (params->xdp_prog)
    wqebbs *= 2;
```
Reason:
This statement modifies the calculation of `wqebbs` to double the reserved space when the XDP program is attached, ensuring that there is enough space in the ICOSQ to accommodate UMR WQEs from both the regular RQ and the XSK RQ, thus preventing potential overflows.
